newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss set short list for air-tracking system bids.
newsitem.headline: Swiss set short list for air-tracking system bids.

text.p: Switzerland's defence ministry has chosen two finalists in the competition to provide a 650 million Swiss franc airspace tracking system for the military, the army's armaments director said on Monday.

The SDA news agency quoted Toni Wicki as saying Berne would decide around mid-year whether to select a consortium comprising Hughes Aircraft Co and Siemens AG's Swiss unit or one comprising Thomson-CSF and Contraves, a unit of Oerlikon-Buehrle Holding AG.
The 1998 budget earmarks 450 million to 500 million francs for the Florako system, which is planned to replace the current outmoded system in phases from the year 2001.
Wicki said the competitors had submitted final offers and that an evaluation of price/performance ratios would decided the winner, SDA reported.
Swiss officicals were not immediately available to confirm the report.
